Halima: Arabic, 'gentle, patient, forbearing'. Halima was the Prophet Muhammad's wet nurse.
Lexie: English pet form of Alexandra or Alexis, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Ariane: French form of Ariadne, Greek 'most holy' or 'very pure'. In myth, she helped Theseus escape the labyrinth.
Charlize: Modern feminine form of Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'. Popularised by actress Charlize Theron, of Afrikaans-French background.
Jannat: Arabic, 'gardens, paradise'. Common among Muslim families.
Dania: Arabic 'near, close', also Hebrew 'God is my judge' (feminine of Dan). Also a Latin name for Denmark.
Andréa: French form of Andrea, from Greek andreios 'manly, brave'. In France and Belgium used for both sexes; here listed for a boy.
Ayana: Several origins: Ethiopian 'beautiful flower', Hebrew 'gazelle', Sanskrit 'path'. Used in various cultures.
Vincent: Latin Vincentius, from vincere 'to conquer'. Saint Vincent is a popular martyr.
Ugo: Italian form of Hugh, from Germanic hug 'mind, spirit'.
Bruno: Germanic, 'brown' or 'armour, protection'. Saint Bruno founded the Carthusian order.
Safae: Arabic Safaa, 'purity, clarity, serenity'. Spelling common in Morocco.
Jakob: German, Dutch and Scandinavian form of Jacob, from Hebrew Yaakov 'supplanter'.
Zara: Arabic 'blooming, radiance', also Hebrew 'dawn' or a short form of Sarah. Used widely in Europe.
Nio: Probably a modern coined name; possibly short form of Antonio or Japanese 'guardian king'. Origin uncertain.
Guus: Dutch short form of Gustaaf (Gustav), from Swedish 'staff of the Goths', or of Augustus.
Rachelle: French form of Rachel, Hebrew 'ewe'. Biblical wife of Jacob.
Miray: Turkish, 'princess, noble lady'. Also from Mir and Ay.
Nyo: Probably a modern coined name, perhaps a variant of Nio. Origin uncertain.
Ayah: Arabic, 'sign, miracle, verse of the Qur'an'. Also Hebrew 'falcon'.
Neva: Spanish 'snow', also Slavic river name in Saint Petersburg, and Welsh variants. Several origins.
Evelina: Latinised form of Eveline, from Norman French from Germanic avi, perhaps 'desired'. Origin partly uncertain.
Hélène: French form of Helen, from Greek helene, possibly 'torch' or 'shining light'.
Karim: Arabic, 'generous, noble'. One of the names of God.
Johanna: Latinised feminine of Johannes, from Hebrew Yochanan 'God is gracious'.
Lison: French diminutive of Élisabeth or Louise. Elisabeth means 'my God is an oath' in Hebrew.
Eduard: German, Dutch and Slavic form of Edward, from Old English 'wealthy guardian'.
Jane: English feminine form of John, via French Jehanne, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Leonard: Germanic, from leon 'lion' and hard 'brave, hardy'. Saint Leonard patron saint of prisoners.
Elora: Probably a modern coined name, or from the Indian Ellora caves. Origin uncertain.
Juno: Latin, the Roman queen of the gods, wife of Jupiter. Origin of the name is uncertain.
Zion: Hebrew, the hill in Jerusalem, a symbol of the promised land. Meaning of the root is unclear.
Jeroom: Flemish form of Jerome, from Greek Hieronymos 'sacred name'.
Mads: Danish short form of Mathias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Yusra: Arabic, 'ease, prosperity'. Often a girl's name in Muslim communities.
Rio: Spanish and Portuguese, 'river'. Also Japanese uses; popularised by the city Rio de Janeiro.
Louelle: Modern French coined name, blend of Lou (Louise) and the suffix -elle. Origin uncertain.
Arno: Germanic short form of Arnold, from arn 'eagle'. Also an Italian river.
Cédric: Invented by Walter Scott in Ivanhoe, probably a misspelling of the Old English Cerdic. Origin uncertain.
Anouk: Dutch and French pet form of Anna, Hebrew 'grace'.
Bo: Scandinavian, from Old Norse búa 'to live', or 'commander'; also English from Bo Derek and Chinese 'precious'. Used for girls in Flanders.
Alyssa: English, possibly from alyssum 'sweet flower', or a variant of Alice. Origin partly uncertain.
Klara: German, Dutch and Scandinavian form of Clara, from Latin clarus 'bright, clear'.
Nadia: Slavic 'hope', Arabic 'caller, moist'. Also Italian variant. Multi-origin name.
Gaël: French and Breton, from Gaël 'Gael', related to Gaelic. In Brittany associated with Saint Gael.
Nelson: English, from a surname meaning 'son of Neil', Gaelic 'champion'. Famous as Admiral Nelson.
Elin: Scandinavian and Welsh form of Helen, from Greek 'torch'.
Antonia: Feminine of Antonius, a Roman family name of uncertain, possibly Etruscan, origin.
Suzan: Variant of Susan, from Hebrew shoshanna 'lily'. Also a Turkish form.
Eliano: Italian, a form of Elian or Elias, or from Latin Aelianus. Origin partly uncertain.
Thelma: Probably coined by novelist Marie Corelli in 1887, perhaps from Greek thelema 'will'. Origin uncertain.
Eliz: Turkish, from a short form of Elizabeth or Eliza. Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Hawa: Arabic and African form of Eve, 'air, breath of life'. Common in West Africa.
Ayline: Turkish, from ay 'moon' and line, 'moonlight'. Used in Turkey and by Turkish communities.
Gennaro: Italian, from Latin Ianuarius 'of January', linked to the god Janus. Saint Gennaro is patron of Naples.
Lévi: Hebrew, 'joined, attached'. A son of Jacob and founder of the tribe of Levites.
Seth: Hebrew, 'appointed' or 'placed'. The third son of Adam and Eve.
Selin: Turkish, 'flowing water, stream' or from Selene, Greek 'moon'.
Luana: Probably a blend of Lu and Anna, or Hawaiian 'enjoyment'. Origin uncertain.
Faustine: French, from Latin Faustina, feminine of Faustus 'fortunate, lucky'.
Noham: Modern French form, probably from Noah or Hebrew 'pleasantness'. Origin uncertain.
Garance: French, 'madder', the red dye plant. Also from Old French garance for the colour red.
Evelyn: English, from Norman French Aveline, from Germanic avi 'desired'; also a surname.
André: French form of Andrew, from Greek andreios 'manly, brave'.
Aminata: West African form of Amina, Arabic 'trustworthy, faithful'. Common in Senegal, Guinea, Mali.
Liliana: Italian, Spanish and Slavic, derived from Latin lilium 'lily', or a form of Elizabeth.
Achilles: Greek, probably 'pain of the people'. Hero of the Trojan War; also Flemish Achiel.
Liva: Latvian and Scandinavian, possibly from Old Norse 'protection', or Latin 'livid'. Origin partly uncertain.
Ode: Probably from Germanic aud 'wealth, fortune', or Greek 'song'. Also a rare Flemish name. Uncertain.
Maylone: Probably a modern coined name, perhaps a blend of May or Malone. Origin uncertain.
Nouri: Arabic, 'my light', from nur 'light'. Also a surname.
Almas: Arabic and Persian, 'diamond'. Also Turkish and Hungarian 'diamond' or 'dream'.
Oussayd: Arabic, a form of Usayd, diminutive of asad 'lion'. Spelling common in Morocco.
Dylan: Welsh, 'son of the sea' or 'great tide'. A sea god in Welsh mythology.
Mélina: French form of Melina, from Greek meli 'honey' or Latin melinus 'yellow'.
Émilie: French form of Emily, from Latin Aemilia, a Roman family name possibly from aemulus 'rival'.
Lima: Possibly Arabic 'a form of ceylon', or Spanish place name. Also a Basque variant. Origin uncertain.
Louen: Breton, a form of Louis or Lowen, Cornish 'joyful'. Origin uncertain.
Ian: Scottish form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Miguel: Spanish and Portuguese form of Michael, Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Mattis: Scandinavian and German form of Matthias, Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Matéo: French form of Mateo, from Hebrew Matityahu 'gift of God'.
Selina: From Latin Caelina or Greek selene 'moon'. Also Turkish Selin variants.
Giuliano: Italian form of Julian, from Latin Iulianus, 'of Julius'.
Matias: Scandinavian, Spanish and Finnish form of Matthias, Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Haron: Arabic form of Harun, Aaron, probably from Hebrew 'mountain' or 'exalted'. Origin debated.
Jax: Modern English, short form of Jackson, meaning 'son of Jack'. Also Jack, Hebrew 'supplanter'.
Louison: French, a diminutive of Louis or Louise, from Germanic hlud 'famous' and wig 'battle'.
Athena: Greek, the goddess of wisdom and war. The meaning of the name is unknown.
Lizio: Probably a modern variant of Lizzio or Elisio, from Elisha or Lisa. Origin uncertain.
Viv: Short form of Vivian or Vivienne, from Latin vivus 'alive'.
Gilles: French form of Giles, from Greek aigidion 'young goat' or 'shield-bearer'. Saint Giles is a hermit saint.
Anthony: English form of Antonius, a Roman family name of uncertain origin. Also linked to Greek anthos 'flower'.
Jill: English short form of Gillian, itself a form of Julian or Juliana, from Latin Iulius.
Gauthier: French form of Walter, from Germanic wald 'rule' and hari 'army'.
Anaëlle: Breton, from Hebrew Hannah 'grace' with the suffix -elle. Modern French coined name.
Adeline: French, a diminutive of Adèle, Germanic adal 'noble'.
Briek: Flemish short form of Fabrice or Cornelius, or possibly Brecht. Origin uncertain.
Florine: French diminutive of Flore or Florence, Latin florens 'blossoming'.
Christian: Latin Christianus, 'follower of Christ'. Greek Christos means 'anointed'.
Khalid: Arabic, 'eternal, immortal'. Khalid ibn al-Walid was a famous companion and general.
Léandro: Spanish and Portuguese variant of Leander, Greek 'lion man' or 'man of the people'.
Hazel: English, from the hazel tree. Used as a first name since the 19th century.
Lexi: Short form of Alexandra or Alexis, from Greek 'defender'.
Julius: Latin Iulius, a Roman family name; possibly 'youthful' or linked to Jupiter.
Aliénor: French form of Eleanor, as in Eleanor of Aquitaine. The origin is disputed; may be 'the other Aenor'.
Oumar: West African spelling of Umar, Arabic, possibly 'long-lived' or 'flourishing'.
Adonis: Greek form of Semitic adon 'lord'. A beautiful youth in Greek mythology.
Yazan: Arabic, possibly from an old South Arabian name. Used in the Levant. Meaning uncertain.
Rosalia: Latin, from rosa 'rose' or rosalia, the Roman festival of roses. Saint Rosalia is the patron of Palermo.
Jonathan: Hebrew Yehonatan, 'God has given'. The friend of David in the Bible.
Wannes: Flemish short form of Johannes, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Ben: Short form of Benjamin ('son of the right hand', Hebrew) or Benedict. Also Hebrew 'son'.
Mehmet: Turkish form of Muhammad, Arabic 'praised, praiseworthy'.
Alec: Scottish short form of Alexander, Greek 'defender of men'.
Soumaya: Arabic Sumayya, 'high, exalted'. Sumayya bint Khayyat was the first martyr of Islam.
Adriano: Italian and Portuguese form of Adrian, Latin Hadrianus, 'from Hadria'.
Stefan: German, Slavic and Dutch form of Stephen, Greek stephanos 'crown, garland'.
Bianca: Italian, 'white, pure'. Also the Italian form of Blanche.
Luisa: Italian, Spanish and German form of Louise, from Germanic hlud 'famous' and wig 'battle'.
Flynn: Irish surname, from Ó Floinn, 'descendant of Flann', meaning 'red' or 'ruddy'.
Maïa: Greek 'good mother', Latin goddess of spring, also Basque and Hebrew uses. Breton variant of Maia.
Nomi: Short form of Naomi, Hebrew 'pleasantness'. Also Japanese 'beautiful'.
Emiliano: Italian and Spanish form of Aemilianus, from the Roman family name Aemilius.
Meyra: Turkish, a variant of Mira or Meyra from Arabic mayra 'fresh, sweet'. Origin partly uncertain.
Miles: English, perhaps from Latin miles 'soldier' or Germanic mil 'merciful'. Origin uncertain.
Donna: Italian, 'lady', from Latin domina. Used as an English given name in the 20th century.
Noralie: Probably a modern blend of Nora and Alie, or Noralie as a variation of Eleonora. Origin uncertain.
Mae: English, a variant of May, from the month or a short form of Mary or Margaret. Also Thai 'mother'.
Tala: Arabic 'palm tree blossom' or 'tall palm', also Filipino 'star'. Multi-origin name.
Ayliz: Turkish, from ay 'moon' and a suffix; also a variant of Ayliz as 'moon trace'. Probably Turkish; uncertain.
Laurens: Dutch form of Laurence, from Latin Laurentius 'of Laurentum', perhaps 'laurel'.
Aurélien: French, from Latin Aurelianus, meaning 'golden', after the Roman family name Aurelius.
Rebecca: Hebrew Rivka, perhaps 'to tie, bind'. Wife of Isaac in the Bible.
Elize: Variant of Elise or Eliza, short form of Elizabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Joanna: Latinised Johanna, from Hebrew Yochanan 'God is gracious'.
Alexandru: Romanian form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Rosanne: Blend of Rose and Anne, or a variant of Roseanna. Latin rosa 'rose' and Hebrew 'grace'.
Sue: Short form of Susan or Susanne, from Hebrew shoshanna 'lily'.
Obe: Frisian short form of old Germanic names such as Obbe, from aud 'wealth' or 'Obert'. Origin uncertain.
Télio: Probably a modern French variant of Thélio, perhaps from Greek Helios 'sun'. Origin uncertain.
Aryan: Sanskrit and Persian, 'noble'. Also an Indian given name. The term has historical associations.
Ousmane: West African form of Uthman, Arabic perhaps 'baby bustard'.
Éloïse: French, possibly from Germanic 'hale, healthy' and 'wide' or from Héloïse; origin disputed.
Anayah: Arabic and Hebrew forms, 'care, concern' (Arabic), and 'God answers' (Hebrew Anaya). Origin partly uncertain.
Matisse: French surname from Mathis, a short form of Mathieu, Hebrew 'gift of God'. Famous painter Henri Matisse.
Daria: Latin feminine of Darius, Persian 'possessing good'. Also Slavic.
Cis: Dutch and Flemish short form of Franciscus or Cornelis. Francis means 'Frenchman'.
Alisa: Variant of Alice or Alyssa, Germanic 'noble kind'. Also Russian Alisa.
Twan: Dutch short form of Antonius (Anthony). Also Frisian Tuan, an Anthony variant.
Ibrahima: West African form of Ibrahim, Abraham, Hebrew 'father of many'.
Mao: Chinese 'hair, fur, hairy', also Japanese 'real, true' and a Spanish pet name. Rare in Belgium; origin uncertain.
Layana: Probably a modern coined name; maybe from Layla or Liana. Origin uncertain.
Jacqueline: French feminine diminutive of Jacques, from Hebrew Yaakov 'supplanter'.
Zoya: Slavic, from Greek zoe 'life'. Also Arabic/Urdu 'loving'.
Liyam: Probably from Hebrew li-yam 'to the sea', or a variant of Liam. Origin uncertain.
Ella-June: Modern English compound of Ella, Germanic 'all, other', and June, the month, from Roman goddess Juno.
Ezekiel: Hebrew Yechezkel, 'God strengthens'. A major prophet in the Old Testament.
Adriel: Hebrew, 'flock of God' or 'God is my majesty'. Biblical Adriel is Saul's son-in-law.
Thibaut: French form of Theobald, from Germanic theud 'people' and bald 'bold'.
Kenzo: Japanese, 'strong and healthy' or 'wise'. Also a shortened form of Kenzō.
Anton: German, Dutch and Slavic form of Antonius, a Roman family name of uncertain origin.
Maëva: Breton coined name, perhaps from Tahitian maeva 'welcome'. Popular in France.
Milla: Short form of Camilla, Amelia or Slavic names with 'mil' meaning 'dear'.
Antonio: Italian and Spanish form of Antonius, a Roman family name of uncertain origin.
Leïla: French spelling of Leila, Arabic 'night', or Persian 'dark-haired'.
Berre: Flemish, from Bernard 'bear' plus 'hard, brave', or from Berre 'bear'. Origin partly uncertain.
Patrick: Latin Patricius, 'nobleman, patrician'. Saint Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland.
Kian: Irish short form of Cian 'ancient', or Persian 'kingly'. Multi-origin name.
Nicole: French feminine of Nicolas, Greek 'victory of the people'.
Eda: Turkish, 'courtesy, manners, grace'. Also Germanic short form of Edith or Edda.
Medina: Arabic, 'city', the holy city of Islam. Also a Spanish surname.
Isolde: Celtic and Germanic, possibly Welsh Essylt 'fair to look at' or 'the one who is gazed at'. Heroine of Tristan and Isolde.
Francis: From Latin Franciscus, 'Frenchman' or 'free man'. Associated with Saint Francis of Assisi.
Ishak: Turkish and Arabic form of Isaac, Hebrew 'he laughs'.
Liano: Probably a modern variant of Lian or Liam, or Italian Liana. Origin uncertain.
Gabriele: Italian form of Gabriel (for boys), Hebrew 'God is my strength'. In German and Dutch for girls.
Raoul: French form of Radulf, from Germanic rad 'counsel' and wulf 'wolf'.
Artur: Portuguese, Polish and Catalan form of Arthur, possibly Celtic 'bear' or 'stone'.
Luz: Spanish, 'light'. Short for Maria de la Luz, 'Our Lady of Light'.
Nahel: Arabic, 'one who drinks', or 'fountain, spring'. Spelling common in France.
Thierno: West African (Fula), a title for a Muslim teacher or scholar. Often a given name in Guinea and Senegal.
Cody: Irish surname from Ó Cuidighthigh 'descendant of the helper', or Old English 'cushion'. Popularised by Buffalo Bill Cody.
Georgia: Feminine form of George, Greek georgos 'farmer'. Also the US state and Caucasian country.
Miral: Arabic or Turkish form of Mira, perhaps 'prince' or 'peace'. Origin uncertain.
Odard: Old Germanic, from aud 'wealth' and hard 'brave, hardy'. Very rare, a French and Walloon saint's name.
